text:
[Item 1: Hangzhou-Beijing travel expenses for attending project seminar (intercity transportation, lodging, meal subsidy, city transportation)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the Business Trip Report Form has been completed with the unit head's signature and the department's official seal. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether this trip was taken by the unit head personally (which would require countersignature by another leader). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether it was a round trip from Hangzhou to Beijing for an official project seminar. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — The rank-based lodging standard: bureau-director-level for Beijing is RMB 650 per night (per Appendix 1, Beijing entire municipality). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Compute — Lodging limit verification: hotel rate RMB 600 per night vs. bureau-director-level Beijing standard of RMB 650 per night. 600 <= 650, within limit. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether intercity transportation and lodging invoices are attached. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Whether transportation class complies with Rule 7(2) for bureau-director-level personnel (train soft sleeper / first-class soft seat / first-class high-speed seat / second-class ship / economy class airfare are eligible). Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Whether there is any situation requiring special explanation (remote area without receipts, no lodging invoice, external unit bearing expenses) — none applies. Result: PASS.
Step 9: Check — Whether meal subsidy conditions under Rule 7(6) are met: both intercity transportation and lodging invoices are present, and no external unit bears these expenses. Result: PASS.
Step 10: Compute — Meal subsidy calculation: 3 calendar days × RMB 100/day (Beijing is not Xinjiang/Qinghai/Tibet) = RMB 300. Claimed amount matches. Result: PASS.
Step 11: Check — Whether meal subsidy is within the standard of Rule 7(8): RMB 100 per person per day for other regions (Beijing). Result: PASS.
Step 12: Check — Whether city transportation is reimbursed against actual invoices (Rule 7(9) permits either invoice-based reimbursement or lump-sum of RMB 80/day). Result: PASS.
Step 13: Check — Whether self-driving or car rental is involved (Rule 7(10) prohibits lump-sum city transportation allowance in such cases) — none involved. Result: PASS.
Step 14: Check — Whether lodging is within Rule 7(3) standard based on Appendix 1 for Beijing at bureau-director level (RMB 650). Result: PASS.
Step 15: Conclusion — All Rule 7 conditions are satisfied: proper approvals, valid invoices, compliant lodging rate and transportation class, properly calculated meal subsidy and city transportation. The expense item is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Post-seminar purchase of routine office supplies (office stationery, newspapers, magazines)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the items (office stationery, newspapers, magazines) are routine office supplies that do not meet the fixed asset threshold. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the items fall within the Asset Management Office's review scope for externally purchased inventory. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the seller provided a goods list together with the invoice (Rule 6(2) requires a goods list from the seller when items do not fall within the Asset Management Office review scope). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether books or other items triggering Rule 6(3) (single book/set ≥ RMB 1,000 requiring library registration) are involved. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether online shopping transaction records are involved (Rule 6(2) alternatively permits online transaction detail record) — none involved. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether the case involves books and materials, printing and production, page charges, or monograph publication subsidies that would require Rule 6(3)-(6) treatment. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Whether the items fall under fixed asset classification (unit price > RMB 1,000 or bulk items with service life > 1 year) — not reached. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Whether the invoice amount exceeds RMB 1,000, which would trigger Rule 6(5) detailed list requirement for photocopying/printing — not applicable (this is office supplies, not printing). Result: PASS.
Step 9: Conclusion — The items qualify as routine office supplies under Rule 6(1); since they are not within the Asset Management Office review scope, the seller's goods list with the invoice satisfies Rule 6(2); no books/printing/publishing involved. The expense is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Maintenance expenses for large centrifuge]
Step 1: Check — Whether maintenance application was submitted through the Asset Management Office system and the Fixed Asset Maintenance Application Form was printed. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the Fixed Asset Maintenance Application Form bears signatures of relevant personnel. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the form has been affixed with the official seal of the affiliated school/unit. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the original invoice for the maintenance service is fully attached. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether the invoice is a negative-list invoice (per Rule 4); the case does not indicate any of the listed deficiencies (no supervision seal mismatch, no scope/content mismatch, no incomplete information, no missing financial seal, no words/figures inconsistency, no alterations, no incomplete procedures). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether the general material requirements under Rule 3 are met (reservation reimbursement form with PI and handler signatures; invoice signed by PI and handler; no contract required since this is a maintenance fee, not an asset purchase, and amount is below the RMB 30,000 single-payment contract threshold). Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — All Rule 17 specific requirements and Rule 3 general requirements are satisfied; the maintenance expense is reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Routine office supplies (office stationery, newspapers, magazines) for recording the maintenance ledger]
Step 1: Check — Whether the items qualify as routine office supplies under Rule 6(1): the case states office stationery, newspapers, and magazines, all explicitly listed as examples in Rule 6(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the items fall within the Asset Management Office's review scope for purchased inventory: the case states they do not, which aligns with Rule 6(2) allowing attachment of a seller-provided goods list. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether a goods list provided by the seller (or online transaction record) is attached: the case confirms the seller provided a goods list with the invoice. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the invoice complies with Rule 4 negative-list requirements (supervision seal, scope matching, complete information, financial seal, consistent amounts, no alterations): no deficiencies are indicated. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether the case involves books/materials, printing/production, or publication contracts requiring additional documentation under Rule 6(3), 6(4), 6(5), or 6(6): the case explicitly states no such materials are involved. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether the payment method complies with Rule 2 (cash management): the amount is not stated in the case, but the case explicitly notes there is no online shopping transaction record. If the single invoice or consecutively numbered invoices exceed RMB 1,000, a POS card slip, online payment certificate, or similar proof must be attached; absence of such proof is a deficiency. Result: FAIL.
Step 7: Check — Whether the general requirements under Rule 3 are met: the case does not describe the reservation reimbursement form, PI/handler signatures on the invoice, or the single-signature approver's signature for university-allocated funds. Result: FAIL.
Step 8: Conclusion — While the office supplies themselves qualify as office expenses with the required goods list attached, key procedural information is missing from the case description (specifically the reservation form, required signatures, payment method proof for amounts potentially exceeding RMB 1,000). Per the audit criteria, when an obviously conditional or essential material is missing, the judgment should be 'Not Reimbursable' rather than 'Pending'. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Final settlement payment for university history museum renovation (engineering project)]
Step 1: Check — Original 'Fudan University Approval Form for Engineering Project Payments and Large Cash Fund Payments' approved by Capital Construction Office is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Approval form bears the official seal of 'Fudan University Capital Construction Office' and the 'Project Review Seal of Fudan University Renovation Management Office'. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Since the project exceeds RMB 100,000, the approval form bears the signature of the director of the Capital Construction Office and the vice president in charge. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Payment is the final settlement payment upon project completion, so the originals of the 'Fudan University Construction Project Cost Review Opinion' and the 'Fudan University Construction Project Final Settlement Audit Filing Form' must be attached. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — The cost review opinion is reviewed by the cost review company with its official seal and bears the 'Capital Construction Office Review Process' seal. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — The final settlement audit filing form bears the signature/seal of the project management department and the receipt acknowledgement and handling opinion of the Audit Office. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Payment amount is controlled according to the contract and project progress, with no overpayment, and the final price is based on the 'approved total settlement amount' and does not exceed the contract price. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — All engineering settlement requirements under Rule 14 are met; no missing approvals, seals, or signatures; amount is properly controlled. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Domestic official hospitality reception expenses (9 visitors, 3 accompanying staff)]
Step 1: Check — Reimbursement documents must include financial invoices, an official letter from the visiting institution, the 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality List,' and the 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form'. Result: FAIL.
Step 2: Check — The case states that 'either the official letter or the Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form was missing'. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — Number of guests is 9 and accompanying staff is 3, which does not exceed the limit of 3 accompanying diners when guests are 10 or fewer. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Working meal standard of RMB 100 per person per day does not exceed the RMB 100 ordinary meal standard. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Banquet standard of RMB 150 per person per occasion does not exceed the RMB 150 per person standard for one working meal/banquet. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — No lodging expense claimed separately, complying with the rule that accommodation expenses shall not be charged for official activities. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — While the quantitative standards (meal/banquet/accompaniment) are met, a key required document (official letter from the visiting institution or the Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form) is missing, making the item not reimbursable in its current form. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Remuneration: Master's thesis defense and academician lecture/consulting fees]
Step 1: Check — Master's thesis reviewer fee: 3 reviewers at RMB 300 each falls within the permitted range of RMB 200–300 per person (Rule 13(1)). Result: FAIL.
Step 2: Check — Master's thesis defense committee: 5 members at RMB 300 each falls within the permitted range of RMB 200–300 per person (Rule 13(1)). Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — Master's thesis defense secretary: 1 secretary at RMB 100 complies with the standard of RMB 100 per person (Rule 13(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Reviewer and defense committee fees exceed the maximum permitted (RMB 300 each, but the rule caps at RMB 300; actually equal to the upper limit — recheck). Result: RMB 300 is at the upper bound of RMB 200–300, so it is within the range.
Step 5: Re-evaluate — Master's thesis reviewer fee of RMB 300 is within the RMB 200–300 range; PASS. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Re-evaluate — Defense committee member fee of RMB 300 is within the RMB 200–300 range; PASS. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Defense committee had 5 members; Rule 13(1) permits 3 to 5 defense committee members for master's thesis — 5 is within range. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Number of reviewers (3) for master's thesis is within the permitted range of 2 to 3. Result: PASS.
Step 9: Check — Academician lecture fee claimed at RMB 1,400 per class hour; Rule 13(2) caps academician lecture fees at generally not exceeding RMB 1,500 per class hour. Result: PASS.
Step 10: Check — Lecture covers 4 class hours total; maximum is 4 class hours per half day; the case does not clearly indicate whether 4 class hours is within a single half day or across multiple days, but assuming a single half day, 4 is the maximum allowed. Result: PASS.
Step 11: Check — Expert consulting by communication paid at RMB 80 per project; Rule 13(3) sets written or remote consultation at RMB 60–100 per project for senior professionals — RMB 80 is within range. Result: PASS.
Step 12: Check — Total master's thesis defense remuneration: 3 reviewers × 300 + 5 defense members × 300 + 1 secretary × 100 = 900 + 1500 + 100 = 2500 RMB. Result: RMB 2,500 within standards.
Step 13: Check — Academician lecture fee: 4 class hours × 1,400 = 5,600 RMB; within cap of 4 × 1,500 = 6,000. Result: PASS.
Step 14: Check — Expert consulting fee: RMB 80 per project, within the RMB 60–100 range. Result: PASS.
Step 15: Conclusion — All labor service fees comply with Rule 13 standards and Rule 12 declaration requirements (assuming standard procedures are followed); the item is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Professor Wang's domestic travel expenses (3-day trip with lodging and meals)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the Fudan University Business Trip Report Form is completed, signed by the unit head, and affixed with the official seal. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether intercity transportation invoices and lodging invoices are provided as required. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the traveler is responsible for claiming meal allowance and local transportation only when intercity transportation and lodging are self-borne (not borne by another institution). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the trip is a self-paid trip (lodging and intercity transportation are self-borne), making meal allowance and local transportation allowable. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Compute — Meal allowance: 3 natural calendar days × RMB 100/day (other regions) = RMB 300; matches the claimed amount. Result: 300.
Step 6: Compute — Local transportation: actual basis reimbursed at RMB 180 (below the lump-sum cap of 80 × 3 = 240); meets the standard. Result: 180.
Step 7: Check — Whether lodging rate of RMB 600/night complies with Appendix 1 limits (destination city not specified; assume a typical city, Bureau-Director-level professor standard around 480–500/night). Result: FAIL.
Step 8: Compute — For Bureau-Director-level Professor Wang, typical lodging standard (e.g., Shanghai other areas 600, most cities 480, Beijing 650). Without the destination city specified, but if the destination is a typical non-first-tier city, RMB 600 may exceed the standard; the rule requires reimbursement within the standard limit. Result: Partially Reimbursable.
Step 9: Conclusion — The travel expense item meets material and approval requirements. The meal allowance and local transportation portions are within standard. However, the lodging nightly rate of RMB 600 may exceed the destination city's Bureau-Director-level standard, requiring partial deduction. Because the destination city is not specified in the case, the lodging portion is judged Partially Reimbursable pending confirmation. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Conference expenses under research funds (100 participants, 2 days, lodging/meals/other RMB 760 per person per day)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the conference is funded by research project funds, triggering the Interim Measures comprehensive quota under Article 9(1)(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Compute — Comprehensive quota for domestic business conferences under research funds: accommodation 500 + meals 150 + other 100 = RMB 750/person/day; the actual claimed RMB 760/person/day slightly exceeds the standard by RMB 10. Result: 750.
Step 3: Check — The case states lodging ~500, meals ~150, other ~110 per person per day; the 'other' component of 110 exceeds the 100 quota standard. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Whether required conference materials are attached: notice/agenda, budget form, expense details, sign-in sheet, service contract/agreement — all present. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Conference duration: 2 days for domestic business conference, which does not exceed the 2-day limit under Article 9(7). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether the number of days exceeds 2 days (registration + departure ≤ 2 days for domestic business conferences). Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — Because the conference uniformly arranges lodging and meals (organizer-arranged), meal allowance and transportation subsidies during the conference period shall not be paid (Article 7(5)) — Professor Wang's travel portion meal allowance for the conference day should be excluded. Result: FAIL.
Step 8: Conclusion — Conference expense comprehensive quota slightly exceeds the standard (750 vs. 760), and the 'other' component of 110 exceeds the 100 cap. Additionally, since lodging and meals are uniformly arranged by the conference, the meal allowance for the conference day in the travel portion should be deducted. The conference expense item is Partially Reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Small office-supply purchases made before and during the conference (office stationery and computer accessories)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the items (office stationery, computer accessories) fall within office expenses per Article 6(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether a sales list is attached to support the office supplies per Article 6(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — For the first purchase: whether invoice amounts are artificially split to evade the list requirement, which is prohibited under Article 6(5). Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Whether the artificial splitting of invoice amounts triggers the negative list under Article 4(8) (incomplete reimbursement procedures). Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — For the second purchase (office stationery and computer accessories with sales list): whether the materials and amount are complete and compliant. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Conclusion — The first purchase involves artificial splitting of invoices, which is explicitly prohibited and renders that portion Not Reimbursable. The second purchase (office stationery and computer accessories with sales list) complies with the rules and is Reimbursable. Overall, the small-purchase item is Partially Reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Training expenses (comprehensive quota + instructor fees)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the training was reported under bureau-director-level standard (accommodation 400, meals 150, venue/materials/transportation 70, other 30, total 650 RMB/person/day). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether training duration of 20 days is within the 30-day full-quota control threshold. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether required materials are complete: Detailed List of Training Expense Expenditures, trainee list, and training service provider invoices. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Comprehensive quota ceiling for 20 days at bureau-director standard: 650 × 20 = 13,000 RMB/person. For group training, member-class ceiling = 550 × 20 = 11,000 RMB/person. Result: 11000-26000.
Step 5: Check — Whether comprehensive quota portion of the claimed 18,720 RMB (which includes 2,500 instructor fees + 600 lodging + 200 meals + 900 transportation for out-of-town lecturer = 4,200 RMB instructor-related) exceeds the standard. Remaining comprehensive-quota-eligible amount: 18,720 − 2,500 − 1,700 = 14,520 RMB, which exceeds the per-person ceiling and likely requires participant count verification. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Check — Whether instructor fees (2,500 RMB) and out-of-town lecturer's lodging (600 RMB), meals (200 RMB), and transportation (900 RMB) comply with Rule 10(4) — instructor fees calculated separately from tuition and discounted at the relevant standard. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — The comprehensive quota portion needs verification against the actual number of trainees (case does not specify participant count). Instructor fees portion (lecturer fee 2,500 + lecturer lodging/meals/transportation 1,700) appears separately compliant under Rule 10(4). Pending determination depends on number of trainees. Result: Pending.

[Item 2: Travel expenses connected with the training (intercity transportation + lodging)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Business Trip Report Form' with unit-head countersignature and seal is attached. Result: FAIL.
Step 2: Check — Whether business trip approval and itinerary materials are attached. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — Whether intercity transportation receipts and lodging invoices are provided. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether responsible person's signature and official seal are complete. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Rule 10(5): When staff attend training away from campus, conference/training notice shall be provided; if organizer arranges meals and lodging uniformly, no meal allowance or transportation subsidy shall be paid. Whether the training already includes lodging/meals is unclear. Result: PENDING.
Step 6: Conclusion — The key Business Trip Report Form and itinerary documents required by Rule 7(1) are missing. The item cannot be reimbursed without these mandatory documents. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Remuneration — special lecture fees and on-site consulting fees]
Step 1: Check — Lecture fee standard: Rule 13(2) — associate senior ≤ 500 RMB/class hour; full senior ≤ 1,000 RMB/class hour; academician/nationally renowned ≤ 1,500 RMB/class hour. Maximum 4 class hours per half day. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Compute — Claimed lecture fee: 500 × 8 = 4,000 RMB. Whether 500/class hour exceeds the cap depends on the lecturer's technical title (not specified in case). Result: Pending on title.
Step 3: Check — On-site consulting fee standard under Rule 13(3): senior titles 500–800 RMB/day (days 1–2), 300–400 RMB/day from day 3; others 300–500 RMB/day (days 1–2), 200–300 RMB/day from day 3. Two days at 800 RMB/day = 1,600 RMB. Result: PASS (within 800 cap).
Step 4: Check — Whether the lecturer was reported under the category for 'division-level and lower personnel' is consistent with claiming lecture fees up to 500/class hour (which corresponds to associate senior level under Rule 13(2)). The case does not state the lecturer's actual title. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — Whether remuneration for external personnel is transferred through the banking system per Rule 12(1). Result: Pending.
Step 6: Conclusion — On-site consulting fees at 800 RMB/day for 2 days comply with Rule 13(3) ceiling for senior titles. Lecture fees at 500 RMB/class hour for 8 hours require confirmation of associate senior technical title per Rule 13(2); the standard claim depends on the lecturer's actual title which is not provided in the case. Result: Pending.

[Item 4: Small purchases of office stationery and drinking water for course preparation]
Step 1: Check — Whether the items (office stationery and drinking water) fall under office expenses per Rule 6(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the items fall within the Asset Management Office's review scope for purchased inventory. Office stationery and drinking water generally do not, so no Fudan University Purchased Inventory Review Result Confirmation Form is needed per Rule 6(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether a goods list provided by the seller or an online purchase transaction detail record is attached per Rule 6(2). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the total amount exceeds the fixed asset threshold (unit price > 1,000 RMB) or is in large quantities exceeding one year of service life. The case describes 'small purchases' of office stationery and drinking water, suggesting low unit value. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether required signatures (project PI and handling staff) on the reservation form and original invoice are obtained per Rule 3(1) and 3(2). Case does not mention signature details. Result: Pending.
Step 6: Conclusion — The item type, scope, and supporting sales list + invoice comply with Rule 6(1) and 6(2). However, signature and approval details are not explicitly stated; assuming standard reimbursement procedures are followed, the item is reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Family-visit travel expenses (unmarried employee, annual visit to parents)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the applicant qualifies as unmarried faculty visiting parents (once-a-year visit). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether expense is limited to intercity transportation (per Rule 11(3)). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Faculty and Staff Family Visit Application and Approval Form' approved by the department and stamped by the Human Resources Office is attached (Rule 11(4)). Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Conclusion — Missing the mandatory Family Visit Application and Approval Form; key approval material is absent, so the item is not reimbursable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Business trip travel expenses (intercity transportation, lodging, meal allowance, local transportation allowance)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the Business Trip Report Form is signed by the unit head and countersigned by another leader (Rule 7(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether a professor qualifies for first-class train seating under Rule 7(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether lodging of RMB 600/night × 2 nights falls within the bureau-director accommodation limit for the destination city. Result: Pending - destination city not specified in the case; assuming tier-1 city, the limit is RMB 600/500, so RMB 600 is within the limit..
Step 4: Compute — Meal allowance: 3 calendar days × RMB 100/day = RMB 300. Result: 300.
Step 5: Compute — Lump-sum local transportation allowance: 3 calendar days × RMB 80/day = RMB 240. Result: 240.
Step 6: Check — Whether meal allowance and local transportation allowance are payable when lodging was reimbursed (Rule 7(5)/(6)). Conference uniformly arranged lodging/meals; however, this portion is for the trip leg not during the conference period. Assuming the lodging reimbursed here is for non-conference nights, allowance is payable. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — All checks pass; the travel expense claim is consistent with Rule 7 and is fully reimbursable (subject to lodging-limit verification against destination city). Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Domestic management conference expenses (non-research funds, ~100 participants, 1 day)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the conference duration complies with Rule 9(7) for domestic management conferences (≤ 1 day). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the conference materials (agenda, budget form, expense list, sign-in sheet, invoices, etc.) are complete per Rule 9(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Compute — Quota comparison: claimed per person per day = RMB 340 (lodging) + RMB 130 (meals) + RMB 90 (other) = RMB 560. Standard for non-research domestic management conference (Category III/IV) = RMB 340 + RMB 130 + RMB 80 = RMB 550. Result: 560 vs 550.
Step 4: Check — Whether 'other expenses' of RMB 90/person/day exceeds the RMB 80/person/day cap for Category III/IV. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Compute — Exceedance = RMB 10/person/day × 100 participants × 1 day = RMB 1,000 in excess. Result: 1000.
Step 6: Conclusion — Lodging and meals are within the quota, but other expenses exceed the cap; the excess RMB 1,000 must be excluded before reimbursement. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 4: Remuneration: doctoral dissertation defense + bureau-level personnel lecture (4 class hours at RMB 900)]
Step 1: Check — Doctoral defense: whether the fee falls within RMB 300-500 per reviewer/committee member and RMB 150 per defense secretary (Rule 13(1)). Result: Pending - case does not specify the per-person amount for the defense; default assume within range..
Step 2: Check — Lecture fee cap: bureau-level personnel with full senior technical title ≤ RMB 1,000/class hour (Rule 13(2)). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Compute — Lecture fee claimed: 4 class hours × RMB 900 = RMB 3,600. Result: 3600.
Step 4: Check — Class-hour limit: maximum 4 class hours per half day (Rule 13(2)). Whether 4 consecutive class hours complies requires confirmation. Result: Pending - scheduling not specified..
Step 5: Check — Whether the same lecture delivered to multiple classes is being counted only once (Rule 13(2)). Result: Pending - not stated..
Step 6: Check — Whether remuneration is settled via bank transfer and the external personnel information has been registered (Rule 12). Result: Pending - payment channel and external-person information not stated..
Step 7: Conclusion — Lecture fee cap is met, but the case lacks per-person defense fees, class-hour scheduling, and external personnel/payment details. Pending confirmation. Result: Pending.

[Item 1: Overseas travel expenses for attending an international education exhibition in Germany]
Step 1: Check — Whether the 'Approval Document for Overseas Travel or Travel to Hong Kong and Macao' issued by the Foreign Affairs Office is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the overseas expense statement listing registration fee, living allowance, incidental expenses, and transportation is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Traveler's rank: bureau-director-level and above, traveling under research funds — verify applicable airfare class. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Air ticket purchased at first-class standard. For research project funds, Rule 8(3) refers back to Rule 7's transportation class standards. Bureau-director-level personnel are entitled to business-class airfare, NOT first-class. First class is reserved for ministerial-level personnel. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — Whether air tickets and boarding passes are available and signed off by the Overseas Travel Service Center of the Foreign Affairs Office (Rule 8(2)). Result: Pending.
Step 6: Check — Whether expenses are settled by official card or bank transfer (Rule 8(4)). Result: Pending.
Step 7: Check — Whether reimbursement is being filed in a single consolidated batch after returning to China (Rule 8(5)). Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — Air ticket class exceeds the bureau-director-level standard under research funds (which is business class). First-class is only available for ministerial-level or equivalent personnel. The airfare portion is therefore non-reimbursable as claimed, while registration fee, living allowance, incidental expenses, and ground transportation remain reimbursable in principle subject to verifying that the rest of the materials (boarding passes, official-card settlement, Foreign Affairs Office countersignature) are complete. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Domestic management conference expenses (non-research funds)]
Step 1: Check — Conference type identification: domestic management conference, non-research funds → Rule 9(1) 2 and Appendix 2 apply. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Period of units of the conference does not exceed the 1-day limit for domestic management conferences (Rule 9(7)). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Required materials: notice and agenda, budget form, expense details, sign-in sheet, and service contract or agreement — case states all are complete. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Hosting/attendance location: not stated whether primarily Shanghai institutions, but no obvious indication of being outside Shanghai or in a prohibited scenic area; no flags raised. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Compute — Compare actual per-person-per-day standard vs. Rule 9(1) 2 standard for Category III/IV: actual 340 (lodging) + 130 (meals) + 90 (other) = 560; rule standard = 340 + 130 + 80 = 550. 'Other expenses' category exceeds the standard by RMB 10 per person per day. Result: 560 vs. 550 — exceeds by RMB 10/person/day.
Step 6: Check — Whether the items may be adjusted among themselves under the comprehensive quota (Rule 9(1) opening sentence allows inter-item adjustment). Result: PASS.
Step 7: Compute — Total participants ~100 × 1 day = 100 person-days. Excess over standard: 100 × RMB 10 = RMB 1,000 must be excluded. Total claimed = ~100 × 560 = RMB 56,000; reimbursable = ~100 × 550 = RMB 55,000. Result: RMB 55,000 reimbursable / RMB 56,000 claimed.
Step 8: Conclusion — Materials are complete and overall amount is within the comprehensive quota framework, but the 'other expenses' component (RMB 90) exceeds the prescribed standard (RMB 80). The portion attributable to the excess must be excluded. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Purchase of application software (intangible asset)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the item is application software not constituting an indispensable component of related hardware → qualifies as intangible asset under Rule 16(2). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the value is RMB 2,000 or above (Rule 16(2) threshold).
